text:
maria: heads up, eu-west rack-12 got a maintenance taint applied and we just observed a cascade of evictions across AZ B. lots of gpu pods bouncing, app errors. looks like cluster-autoscaler thrash + scheduler placement pushed pods onto the same remaining few racks and those nodes started draining too.
deploy-bot: automated: taint added to nodepool/rack-12: maintenance=planned:NoSchedule by ops-automation (3969991235)
aj: do we have the eviction logs and the pod priority classes? might be a priority inversion where low-priority gpu jobs evict higher-priority sidecars. can you paste `kubectl get pod -o wide` for a couple of hit pods and the node taints?
maria: quick dump below for one victim. small snippets:
```
$ kubectl get pod gpu-train-42 -o jsonpath='{.metadata.name} {.status.phase} {.metadata.annotations}'
gpu-train-42 Running annotation:evicted-by:node/rack-12
$ kubectldescribe node rack-12-node-3 | grep -i Taints -A2
Taints: maintenance=planned:NoSchedule
Conditions: Ready False NetworkUnavailable False
```

toby: that `NetworkUnavailable False` line is weird — I think the taint was applied after some partial network outage and autoscaler saw low allocatable capacity and scaled down warm pools in AZ A, then tried to rebalance into AZ B which was already compacted. TL;DR: autoscaler + taint applied -> scheduler moved lots of pods -> more nodes drained -> loop.
aj: can you check cluster-autoscaler events? `kubectl -n kube-system get events --field-selector involvedObject.kind=Deployment` or CA pod logs. we need to see scale-down decisions.
maria: pasting CA tail:
```
I0323 12:01:23 scale_down.go:102 scaling down nodegroup eu-west-b:1 -> 0, utilization below threshold
I0323 12:01:28 scale_up.go:88 increasing desired=3 -> 4 for nodegroup eu-west-a due to unschedulable pods
I0323 12:01:33 eviction_controller.go:56 Evicting pod gpu-train-42 due to taint maintenance=planned
I0323 12:02:10 scale_down.go:102 scale down candidate eu-west-b:2 -> 1 (emptied nodes)
```

sre-bot: alert: high eviction rate on cluster eu-west (GPU) — 45 evictions in 5m. ticket created: INF-4392

toby: short mitigation: add tolerations to critical system pods (logging, control-plane sidecars) and pin long-running GPU jobs to `gpu-dedicated` taint-tolerant nodepool. also temporarily pause scale-down by setting CA scale-down enabled=false, or bump scale-down-unneeded-time to avoid immediate shrink.
aj: agree. immediate steps I propose: 1) disable CA scale-down for 20m 2) remove taint from rack-12 nodes if maintenance can be postponed: `kubectl taint nodes rack-12-node-* maintenance-` 3) add a PDB for the most critical services so they don't get orphaned.
maria: did the first two, removed taint on rack-12 and set CA scale-down to false. evictions slowed. applying PDBs now.
```
apiVersion: policy/v1
kind: PodDisruptionBudget
metadata:
  name: infra-critical-pdb
spec:
  minAvailable: 1
  selector:
    matchLabels:
      app: infra-critical
```

aj: good. we also need a medium-term fix: scheduler topology-aware soft-affinity for GPU jobs + preferSpread across racks, and a defrag job that consolidates tiny GPU pods into fillable nodes before scale-down. otherwise we'll keep noisy tail effects. plus add a safety valve in autoscaler to avoid cross-az collapse: don't scale-down below X nodes per-az when taints are present.
toby: +1, and add a heuristic in placement: when a rack-level taint applied, treat it as draining window and temporarily increase binpacking bin size tolerance so scheduler avoids packing everything to the same few racks. could implement as controller that patches `PreferAvoidPods` or sets a transient pod anti-affinity.
sre-bot: note logged mitigation actions to INF-4392: taint removed, CA scale-down disabled (20m), PDB created.
maria: follow-up — we saw reduced evictions after taint removal and scale-down pause. some pods are still in CrashLoopBackOff because PVC attachment failed briefly while nodes cycled. working on reattach. estimated full recovery 12:35 UTC.
aj: postmortem actions we should add to backlog: 1) autoscaler az-min-per-az policy 2) rack-taint propagation policy (announce/guardrail) 3) defragmentation job for GPUs 4) docs for ops team before manual taint. assign INF-4392.
maria: noted. cost note: we briefly had 3 low-util GPU nodes left idle after scale down pauses and taint; cost delta ~0.4 GPU-hour but worth for stability this time. will include cost in postmortem.
toby: quick template for the defrag job I sketched (K8s CronJob) — will open PR: basically schedule a controller that looks for tiny gpu pods (<0.25 GPU) and attempts eviction with binpack hints to consolidate before CA scale-down.
aj: please add an integration test for the scenario: apply rack taint while CA is enabled and assert we don't end up with cross-az concentration.
maria: will write the test and attach to INF-4392. thanks all. :heart:
deploy-bot: automated: ticket INF-4392 updated by maria — adds remediation steps and anchors tasks (3969991259)
